objective: Give the read-only dashboard backend an explicit shutdown and overload contract: readiness flips to NOT_READY before termination, new work is refused with a retryable 503, concurrent requests stay bounded, and a wedged handler can never keep the process alive past the drain deadline.
decision_supported: Can the backend drain and refuse work in a defined order - NOT_READY, then refused requests, then a stopped accept loop - while liveness stays up and every refusal is a stable, non-leaking, retryable response?
acceptance: SIGTERM and Ctrl-C stop new requests, drain in-flight work up to a deadline, then exit with status 0
readiness reports NOT_READY before termination while liveness stays up for the duration of the drain
concurrent requests remain bounded and overload returns a stable 503 with Retry-After and no internal detail
writes are refused while draining instead of reaching a read model
a handler that outlives the drain deadline cannot block process exit
the drain deadline is validated and configurable through the CLI and environment
the OpenAPI contract documents the draining and concurrency refusal on every affected route
shutdown does not corrupt logs or the read-model cache
tests cover slow requests, concurrent requests, SIGTERM-equivalent shutdown, and bounded overload
evidence: end-to-end SIGTERM process run showing readiness flipping to not_ready, refused routes and exit status 0
in-flight request output showing the drain waited for work that had already started
wedged-handler output showing the drain deadline was enforced instead of blocking shutdown
overload output showing the bounded 503 with Retry-After at the concurrency limit
targeted pytest output with the collected Issue #93 test names, pass counts and exit codes
make test, make contract, make scenario-check, make golden-check and make context-check output with exit codes
final git diff --check and git diff --name-only output proving every changed path is allowed
stop_conditions: the change would require a control, ROS, MCU, motion or emergency-stop endpoint
the change would require deploying, restarting or reconfiguring a live container or host
readiness would keep reporting ready after termination began
a refusal response would echo read-model contents, filesystem paths or other internals
the change requires modifying the dashboard rendering layer or its fixtures
a required modification falls outside allowed_paths
risks_and_fallbacks: The concurrency bound was already enforced before worker creation; this change keeps that behaviour and extends it with an explicit drain contract.
Refusal is decided in the handler rather than in process_request because only the handler can see the request path, and the life-cycle probes must stay answerable while draining.
In-flight requests are waited for rather than cancelled or truncated, so a client never receives a partial response because shutdown started.
A handler that ignores the deadline is abandoned; daemon worker threads and server_close keep exit bounded, and the drain logs drained=false so the condition is visible rather than silent.
The drain deadline defaults to 5 seconds and is capped at 30 so a misconfigured value cannot stall deployment.
